tool_arguments.query: Microsoft FY2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Microsoft FY2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

Microsoft’s FY2025 Q3 (quarter ended March 31, 2025) capital expenditures, **including finance leases**, were **$21.4 billion**, while cash paid for property, plant, and equipment was **$16.7 billion**. [[1]] 
The roughly **$4.7 billion** difference reflects the quarter’s finance-lease component, principally related to data-center capacity timing. [[1]] 
Management said approximately **half** of cloud- and AI-related spending went to long-lived assets expected to support monetization for **15 years or more**; the other half was primarily CPUs and GPUs used to meet demand signals, including a **$315 billion** contracted backlog. [[1]] 
This was a substantial step-up from FY2024 Q3’s **$14.0 billion** of capex including finance leases—an increase of approximately **53% year over year**—while cash PP&E spending rose from **$11.0 billion** to **$16.7 billion**. [[2]] [[1]] 
Microsoft attributed the Q3 FY2025 amount being slightly below its expectations to normal variability in the timing of data-center lease deliveries, not a reduction in AI infrastructure commitment. [[1]] 
For FY2025 Q4, the company guided that capex would rise sequentially, while maintaining its prior aggregate second-half FY2025 capex outlook. [[1]] 
Management also said AI demand was growing faster than capacity additions and expected some AI capacity constraints to persist beyond June 2025. [[1]] 
For FY2026, Microsoft expected capex to keep growing but at a lower rate than FY2025, with a greater proportion of shorter-lived assets tied more directly to revenue. [[1]]

Sources:
[S1.1] Microsoft Fiscal Year 2025 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call — https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2025/earnings-fy-2025-q3
[S1.2] Microsoft (MSFT) Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2024/04/25/microsoft-msft-q3-2024-earnings-call-transcript/

tool_arguments.query: Alphabet FY2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Alphabet FY2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

**Alphabet’s Q3 FY2025 AI-infrastructure spending accelerated sharply:** reported capital expenditure was **$24.0 billion** for the quarter ended September 30, 2025, versus **$13.0 billion** in Q3 2024—an increase of approximately **85% year over year**. [[1, 2]]

- The “vast majority” of Q3 capex went to **technical infrastructure**, with roughly **60% ($14.4 billion)** directed to **servers** and **40% ($9.6 billion)** to **data-center and networking equipment**. [[1]]
- Alphabet’s 10-Q defines technical infrastructure as servers and network equipment supporting computing, storage, networking—including AI—and data-center land and building construction; therefore, the $24 billion is best viewed as AI-enabled infrastructure spending rather than a company-disclosed, AI-only capex figure. [[3]]
- Google Cloud’s Q3 revenue rose **34% to $15.2 billion**, with growth driven in part by enterprise AI infrastructure and AI solutions, while Cloud backlog increased by **$49 billion sequentially**. [[1]]
- Management said supply would remain tight in Q4 2025 and 2026 despite faster server deployments and data-center construction, underpinning continued aggressive capacity investment. [[1]]

**FY2025 outlook:** Alphabet raised expected full-year capex to **$91–$93 billion**, from its prior **$85 billion** outlook. [[1]] Through the first nine months of 2025, purchases of property and equipment were **$63.596 billion**, compared with **$38.259 billion** in the comparable 2024 period. [[3]]

**Profit-and-cash-flow implications:** Q3 depreciation rose **$1.6 billion year over year to $5.6 billion**, or **41%**, and Alphabet expected depreciation growth to accelerate modestly in Q4 as the enlarged infrastructure base enters service. [[1]] Management also indicated that 2026 capex would increase significantly, with specifics to follow at its Q4 results. [[1]]

Sources:
[S3.1] Alphabet Investor Relations - 2025 Q3 Earnings Call — https://abc.xyz/investor/events/event-details/2025/2025-Q3-Earnings-Call-2025-4OI4Bac_Q9/default.aspx

tool_arguments.query: Amazon FY2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

events.content: Amazon FY2025 Q3 capital expenditure AI data center spending

Amazon’s **Q3 FY2025 cash capital expenditure was $34.2 billion**, versus **$21.3 billion in Q3 FY2024**, a roughly **61% year-over-year increase**. [[1]] [[2]] 

For the first nine months of FY2025, cash CapEx reached **$89.9 billion**, and management raised its FY2025 expectation to approximately **$125 billion**, with spending expected to increase again in 2026. [[1]] 

Management said the spending **primarily relates to AWS**, including capacity for demand in **AI and core cloud services**, custom AI silicon such as **Trainium**, and technology infrastructure that also supports Amazon’s North America and International businesses. [[1]] 

The reported cash-flow-line item, “purchases of property and equipment,” was **$35.095 billion in Q3** and **$92.297 billion year-to-date**; the difference from the $34.2 billion “cash CapEx” figure reflects Amazon’s broader management definition and cash-flow timing/other capital items. [[2]] [[1]] 

The balance-sheet evidence points to a heavily AWS/data-center-oriented buildout: AWS property and equipment, net rose from **$110.7 billion at December 31, 2024** to **$165.1 billion at September 30, 2025**, while Amazon says technology-infrastructure assets are allocated by usage with the **majority allocated to AWS**. [[2]] 

Amazon did not disclose a precise stand-alone “AI data-center” dollar amount for Q3; therefore, the most defensible interpretation is that AI/data-center spending constituted the primary use of the $34.2 billion quarterly cash-CapEx program, rather than treating the entire amount as AI-only spending. [[1]]

Sources:
[S5.1] Amazon (AMZN) Q3 2025 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2025/10/31/amazon-amzn-q3-2025-earnings-call-transcript/

tool_arguments.query: Meta FY2025 Q3 earnings call capital expenditure AI infrastructure

events.content: Meta FY2025 Q3 earnings call capital expenditure AI infrastructure

**Meta’s latest FY2026 capital-expenditure guidance is $130 billion–$145 billion**, inclusive of principal payments on finance leases; this is the outlook issued with Q2 results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. [[1]] 

The range was narrowed upward from **$125 billion–$145 billion** following Q1, implying a **$5 billion increase at the midpoint**, while the $145 billion upper bound was retained. [[2, 3]] 

For context, Meta initially guided to **$115 billion–$135 billion** for 2026, with year-over-year growth attributed to investment supporting Meta Superintelligence Labs and the core business. [[4]] 

Meta spent **$31.08 billion in Q2 2026** and **$19.84 billion in Q1**, with spending directed to servers, data centers, and network infrastructure. [[1, 5, 2]] 

Management’s stated uses for the AI-infrastructure build include model training, scaling the core advertising/business platform, personal agents and new products, and eventually serving large external customers; it also is laying data-center and network foundations for compute expansion in 2028 and beyond. [[2]] 

The Q1 guidance increase reflected expected higher component prices and, to a lesser extent, incremental data-center costs for future-year capacity. [[6, 3]] 

A useful scale comparison is that Meta’s FY2025 capex was **$72.22 billion**, so the current FY2026 guidance implies an approximately **80%–101% increase year over year**. [[4, 1]] 

The principal analytical takeaway is that Meta is explicitly accepting a near-term cash-flow and depreciation burden to secure AI capacity ahead of demand, rather than sizing infrastructure solely to current utilization; investors should therefore track capex execution, infrastructure-driven operating-expense growth, and evidence of monetization in ads, AI products, and enterprise offerings. [[2, 4]]

Comparative AI-related capex by the four hyperscalers (all FY/quarter ending most recently reported):

- **Microsoft FY2025 Q3** (quarter ended March 31, 2025): $21.4B total capex incl. finance leases; $16.7B cash PP&E. Up 53% YoY from $14.0B in FY2024 Q3. ~half directed to long-lived data-center assets supporting 15+ year monetization; the other half to CPUs/GPUs meeting demand signals, including a $315B contracted backlog. Source: S1.1, S1.2.

- **Alphabet FY2025 Q3** (quarter ended Sept 30, 2025): $24.0B capex, up 85% YoY from $13.0B in Q3 2024. ~60% ($14.4B) to servers, 40% ($9.6B) to data-center/networking. FY2025 guided $91–$93B total capex. Source: S3.1, S3.2, S3.3.

- **Amazon FY2025 Q3** (quarter ended Sept 30, 2025): $34.2B cash capex, up 61% YoY from $21.3B. FY2025 guided ~$125B total, with the majority allocated to AWS AI and core cloud infrastructure (custom Trainium silicon, data‑center capacity). Source: S5.1, S5.2.

- **Meta FY2025 full year**: $72.22B capex. FY2026 guided $130–$145B (+80–101% YoY). Q2 2026 quarterly spend $31.08B; Q1 2026 $19.84B directed to servers, data‑centers, network infrastructure for AI model training, core ads platform, personal agents, and future capacity through 2028+. The magnitude of spending—ranging from ~$21B (Microsoft quarter) to ~$34B (Amazon quarter) and $72B+ (Meta annual)—signals strong, sustained demand for NVIDIA and AMD AI accelerators through 2026 and beyond.

Microsoft’s FY2025 Q3 (quarter ended March 31, 2025) capital expenditures, **including finance leases**, were **$21.4 billion**, while cash paid for property, plant, and equipment was **$16.7 billion**. [[1]] 
The roughly **$4.7 billion** difference reflects the quarter’s finance-lease component, principally related to data-center capacity timing. [[1]] 
Management said approximately **half** of cloud- and AI-related spending went to long-lived assets expected to support monetization for **15 years or more**; the other half was primarily CPUs and GPUs used to meet demand signals, including a **$315 billion** contracted backlog. [[1]] 
This was a substantial step-up from FY2024 Q3’s **$14.0 billion** of capex including finance leases—an increase of approximately **53% year over year**—while cash PP&E spending rose from **$11.0 billion** to **$16.7 billion**. [[2]] [[1]] 
Microsoft attributed the Q3 FY2025 amount being slightly below its expectations to normal variability in the timing of data-center lease deliveries, not a reduction in AI infrastructure commitment. [[1]] 
For FY2025 Q4, the company guided that capex would rise sequentially, while maintaining its prior aggregate second-half FY2025 capex outlook. [[1]] 
Management also said AI demand was growing faster than capacity additions and expected some AI capacity constraints to persist beyond June 2025. [[1]] 
For FY2026, Microsoft expected capex to keep growing but at a lower rate than FY2025, with a greater proportion of shorter-lived assets tied more directly to revenue. [[1]]

Sources:
[S7.1] Microsoft Fiscal Year 2025 Third Quarter Earnings Conference Call — https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/investor/events/fy-2025/earnings-fy-2025-q3
[S7.2] Microsoft (MSFT) Q3 2024 Earnings Call Transcript — https://www.fool.com/earnings/call-transcripts/2024/04/25/microsoft-msft-q3-2024-earnings-call-transcript/

function.arguments: {"query":"Meta FY2025 Q3 earnings call capital expenditure AI infrastructure"}

private_messages.content:
**Meta’s latest FY2026 capital-expenditure guidance is $130 billion–$145 billion**, inclusive of principal payments on finance leases; this is the outlook issued with Q2 results for the quarter ended June 30, 2026. [[1]] 

The range was narrowed upward from **$125 billion–$145 billion** following Q1, implying a **$5 billion increase at the midpoint**, while the $145 billion upper bound was retained. [[2, 3]] 

For context, Meta initially guided to **$115 billion–$135 billion** for 2026, with year-over-year growth attributed to investment supporting Meta Superintelligence Labs and the core business. [[4]] 

Meta spent **$31.08 billion in Q2 2026** and **$19.84 billion in Q1**, with spending directed to servers, data centers, and network infrastructure. [[1, 5, 2]] 

Management’s stated uses for the AI-infrastructure build include model training, scaling the core advertising/business platform, personal agents and new products, and eventually serving large external customers; it also is laying data-center and network foundations for compute expansion in 2028 and beyond. [[2]] 

The Q1 guidance increase reflected expected higher component prices and, to a lesser extent, incremental data-center costs for future-year capacity. [[6, 3]] 

A useful scale comparison is that Meta’s FY2025 capex was **$72.22 billion**, so the current FY2026 guidance implies an approximately **80%–101% increase year over year**. [[4, 1]] 

The principal analytical takeaway is that Meta is explicitly accepting a near-term cash-flow and depreciation burden to secure AI capacity ahead of demand, rather than sizing infrastructure solely to current utilization; investors should therefore track capex execution, infrastructure-driven operating-expense growth, and evidence of monetization in ads, AI products, and enterprise offerings. [[2, 4]]

Sources:
[S8.1] Meta - Meta Reports Second Quarter 2026 Results — https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-Reports-Second-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx
[S8.2] 1 Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) Second Quarter 2026 Results Conference Call — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q2/META-Q2-2026-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf
[S8.3] Meta Reports First Quarter 2026 Results — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/Meta-03-31-2026-Exhibit-99-1_final.pdf

[S8.5] 1 Meta Platforms, Inc. (META) First Quarter 2026 Results Conference Call — https://s21.q4cdn.com/399680738/files/doc_financials/2026/q1/META-Q1-2026-Earnings-Call-Transcript.pdf

Source: S1.1, S1.2.

- **Alphabet FY2025 Q3** (quarter ended Sept 30, 2025): $24.0B capex, up 85% YoY from $13.0B in Q3 2024. ~60% ($14.4B) to servers, 40% ($9.6B) to data-center/networking. FY2025 guided $91–$93B total capex. Source: S3.1, S3.2, S3.3.

- **Amazon FY2025 Q3** (quarter ended Sept 30, 2025): $34.2B cash capex, up 61% YoY from $21.3B. FY2025 guided ~$125B total, with the majority allocated to AWS AI and core cloud infrastructure (custom Trainium silicon, data‑center capacity). Source: S5.1, S5.2.

- **Meta FY2025 full year**: $72.22B capex. FY2026 guided $130–$145B (+80–101% YoY). Source: S8.1–S8.6.

All four hyperscalers are executing multi‑year, double‑digit percentage capex increases, driven primarily by AI‑infrastructure demand (servers, data‑center build‑out, custom AI silicon).
